name: Amos

facts.author: Amos, a herdsman from Tekoa in Judah and a gatherer of sycamore fruit, whom God sent to prophesy to Israel (1:1, 7:14-15).
facts.audience: The northern kingdom of Israel in the days of King Jeroboam the son of Joash

about: Amos was not a professional prophet. He was a farmer from the hills of Judah, but God called him to go north and preach to Israel, two years before a great earthquake (1:1). Israel was rich and at peace. The wealthy lived in fine houses and held religious feasts, but they cheated the poor, took bribes and crushed the needy.

Amos begins by announcing God's judgement on the nations around Israel for their cruelty, and then turns to Judah and finally to Israel itself (2:6). Because God chose Israel, He will hold them to account (3:2). Their worship means nothing to Him without justice and righteousness (5:24).

Amos sees five visions of judgement, and when Amaziah the priest of Bethel tells him to go home, he stands firm (7:10-17). Yet the book ends with hope: God will raise up the fallen house of David and bring His people back to a land of plenty (9:11-15).

themes.title: Justice for the poor
themes.text: God sees how the rich treat the poor, and He will judge those who oppress them.

themes.title: Worship that pleases God
themes.text: Feasts and offerings are hateful to God when the worshippers live unjust lives.

themes.title: Privilege brings responsibility
themes.text: Israel had been specially chosen, so its sin was all the more serious.

themes.title: The Lord of all nations
themes.text: God judges every nation for its wickedness, and in the end He will restore David's kingdom.
